title: VAT and discounts
summary: Add VAT to a price, take it out again, and apply a percentage discount, using rates held in input cells.

blocks.text: The store system holds prices without VAT, but customers see prices with VAT, and marketing wants a sale price on top. You need all three numbers for every item.

In this mission the VAT rate sits in an input cell. The rate used is an example: 16% is Kenya's standard VAT rate, per the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), but rates can change, so always check the current rate before using one in real work. Prices and discounts are fictional.

items: Objective: calculate VAT, price including VAT, and a discounted price using input cells.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.caption: VAT and discount formulas (rate in B1, discount in B2)
rows: price excluding VAT times the VAT rate
price plus the VAT amount (same as =B5*(1+$B$1))
take VAT out of a price that includes it
keep what is left after the discount

blocks.text: Worked example, using an example VAT rate of 16%. A pair is KES 2,000 excluding VAT. VAT is 2,000 x 16% = 320, so the price including VAT is 2,320.

To go backwards, divide, do not subtract. KES 2,320 including VAT is the price times 1.16, so the price excluding VAT is 2,320 / 1.16 = 2,000. Taking 16% off 2,320 gives 1,948.80, which is wrong, because the 16% was worked out on the smaller price.

A discount of 15% leaves 100% - 15% = 85% of the price, so multiply by (1 - 15%). On a price of 2,320 that is 2,320 x 0.85 = 1,972. The brackets matter: the subtraction must happen before the multiplication.
Tip: keep the VAT rate and the discount in input cells and refer to them with $ signs. When the rate changes, change one cell and every price updates. Never type 0.16 into a formula.
Four questions on VAT and discounts. Use the example VAT rate of 16% where a rate is needed. Type numbers without commas.

items: VAT amount = price excluding VAT x rate. Price including VAT = price x (1 + rate).
To remove VAT, divide by (1 + rate). Do not subtract the rate from the bigger price.
A discount keeps (1 - discount) of the price, so multiply by it.
Keep rates in input cells and use $ signs so one change updates every formula.

blocks.text: Next: order of operations, so Excel calculates what you mean.

options.label: Change B1 only, and every price updates

Nothing, because Excel updates the rate itself
